revisions.agent_reply:
`policy.py` is written and evaluates at 112/113 notes (99.1%) on the six training charts, with no errors raised and `plan()` taking about 1 ms per tick.

**Strategy**

*Perception.* Each frame is warped through a homography (fitted against the ground-truth frames with the probe, 2 ms timing error) into a rectified lane × time-to-hit grid. Pixels are classified by colour: cyan taps, green holds, magenta slides. Taps are runs along each lane's centre band. Holds and slides are split into a full-height head (giving the hit time) and a thinner body (giving the duration and, for slides, the lane path per time column). Partially occluded or cut-off heads are flagged as incomplete.

*Tracking.* Detections are matched to tracks by kind, lane, and hit time. Each track keeps a weighted median of its hit time over many frames (complete heads weigh more), so a note stays accurately known after the hand hides it. Body-only detections, including heads stopped on the judgment line while being played, only update durations and slide paths. A new note cannot be created inside a hold already occupying its lane, which stops hold bodies from spawning ghosts.

*Control.* A greedy scheduler walks the tracked notes in time order. Notes due together become chords played with the gripper opened to the lane spacing (1 or 2 lanes apart). For each event it checks whether lift, travel at 1.8 m/s, and descent fit before the hit (allowing up to 60 ms late), scaling hover height and lift/descent times between a rushed and a comfortable motion according to the slack, and skips notes it cannot reach. Once a descent starts the event is committed and carried through regardless of re-planning. Holds and slides stay pressed until their end, with slides following the tracked path 40 ms ahead, and may be released after about 82% plus a margin when the next note needs the hand. While one fingertip holds a note, the other fingertip is rolled up 16 mm and can tap, hold, or slide notes within 2 lanes on its side; this path keeps the held note at 96-100% contact in mechanical tests but no training chart has overlapping notes, so its scoring effect is unverified.

**Not resolved.** The one remaining training miss is lane 1 of a lane 0+1 chord played 0.31 s after a lane 3 tap. Lift height and travel speed did not change it, and the commanded fingertip positions are correct, so I left it. The test hooks (phantom taps, static roll) remain in the file as disabled constants, and a safety fallback returns a hover plan if the controller ever raises.

The revision is done. It now completes 113/113 notes (100%) on the training charts, with no errors, and the changes target denser charts.

**What changed and why**

- **Pair mode for the free fingertip.** When a tap is followed within 0.6 s by a note 1 or 2 lanes away and a lift-travel-descend hop cannot make it, the first tap's fingertip now stays pressed and the other fingertip rolls down onto the second note (tap or hold). This fits notes as close as 0.1 s apart. I forced it on every qualifying training pair as a stress test: all 13 pairs were hit, including two holds played entirely by the free fingertip, which validates the free-tip touch mechanics against the judge for the first time.
- **One-step look-ahead.** A tap is touched up to 50 ms early when the following note would otherwise be unreachable, and the late tolerance grew from 60 to 80 ms. The tap dwell dropped from 50 to 40 ms. Together these fixed the one chord the previous revision missed.
- **Free fingertip after a hold ends.** The held fingertip may stay pressed up to 0.25 s past its note's end so the free fingertip can take a note that follows closely, instead of needing a full hop.
- **Bug fix exposed by the above.** Keeping finished sustains in the note list briefly revealed that a committed sustain past its end was never marked done, which blocked the next note (an interim run dropped to 86%). Fixed by comparing against the release time with a tolerance.

**Caveats.** Pair mode and early-shift only trigger when the normal hop is infeasible, so on the training charts the final run plays exactly as before plus the recovered chord. Timing precision stays tight (hits 8 to 11 ms early, spread 2 to 11 ms). The free-tip path during long holds (taps while holding) is still only validated mechanically, since no training chart overlaps notes that way.

Revision 2 is done. It scores 112/113 (99.1%) on the training charts, with the remaining miss being the lane 0+1 chord that flips between hit and miss from run to run (it was hit in revision 1 and in several interim runs here with near-identical commanded motion), and no errors. The work this round targeted denser, unseen charts.

**What changed and why**

- **Offline dense-chart simulator (probe).** Since training charts are saturated, I built a fake-API simulator in the probe: random dense charts (8th and 16th streams, chords, holds with taps, slides), linear plan playback with a small lag, and a judge model (fresh touches, lanes, hold contact). It categorises misses, which showed streams of notes 0.1 to 0.2 s apart within 2 lanes were the dominant loss. On those charts the policy went from 69.5% to 81.7% completion during this revision.
- **Faster hops.** Minimum lift, descent and dwell dropped to 40, 60 and 30 ms. Rushed hops on the real arm still hit their notes with 2 to 8 ms timing spread.
- **Alternating-fingertip chains.** When consecutive notes come too fast to hop and each lies 1 or 2 lanes from the previous, the two fingertips now take turns: one stays pressed while the other rolls down onto the next note, with lateral moves made while a tip is raised and the same tip allowed to play twice in a row if time permits. Chains may end in a hold. Forced on the training charts, every chained note was hit on the real arm, so the mechanics are validated physically. In the simulator a 0.15 s zigzag is played completely and a 0.09 s one mostly.
- **Fixes found along the way.** Notes kept pressed for a pair or chain now stay in the note list until the run ends (previously the first note dropped out 0.12 s after its hit and the run collapsed), and chains lift immediately after the last note instead of padding.

**Tried and dropped.** Charging gripper-opening time against the hop budget did not fix the flaky chord and cost other chords on the real arm, so it is effectively disabled.

Revision 3 is done: 113/113 (100%) on the training charts in two consecutive runs, no errors, and the dense-chart simulation unchanged at about 81%.

**What changed and why**

- **Gripper opens during the lift, not during travel.** For chords the hand now sets its opening while rising off the previous note, so the width is settled before the fast lateral move and descent. This is what finally fixed the lane 0+1 chord that had been flipping between hit and miss across revisions; it has now hit in two consecutive runs.
- **Lateness cap for short holds.** A note may be touched up to 80 ms late to fit it in, but a late start on a short hold eats into the 80% contact requirement. Sustains now cap their allowed lateness to about 12% of their duration, so a 0.3 s hold is never started more than 25 ms late.
- **Merged same-lane taps split earlier.** Two taps in one lane less than 70 ms apart can merge into one blob; the split threshold dropped from 1.7 to 1.4 note widths so such pairs are detected as two notes instead of one mis-centred note.

**Validation this round**

- **Perception on doubled density.** I composited the note pixels of two training frames into one image and checked detection against the union of their ground truth over 186 pairs: tap, hold and slide recall stayed at 97 to 98%, and the remaining misses were cases my compositing created that cannot occur in a real chart (two notes drawn on top of each other in the same lane).
- **Scheduler.** The offline dense-chart simulator confirmed the scheduling changes cost nothing (81.4% vs 81.7% at the densest setting, within noise).

Revision 4 is done: 113/113 (100%) on the training charts, no errors, and the dense-chart simulation improved from 81.4% to 83.5%.

**What changed and why** (all found by tracing misses in the offline dense-chart simulator)

- **Partner notes are released when a pair or chain cannot start.** When the first note of a pair or chain was unreachable, the whole group was skipped, including notes the other fingertip could still have played on its own. A trace showed a tap plus a 1.1 s hold both lost even though the hold alone was easily reachable. Now the partner notes are freed and planned normally.
- **Fast slides hold their start lane until the touch registers.** The hand used to begin following the slide path 40 ms ahead immediately, so on fast slides (the training set has ones moving 2 lanes in 0.1 s) the fingertip could touch down already outside the start lane and the hit would not count. The hand now stays on the start lane for 40 ms after the touch keyframe, then follows the path. Real-arm slide contact and lateral error are unchanged (98 to 100%, 7 to 10 mm).
- **Chains may take one note of an unreachable chord.** If a chord follows a fast run too closely for the hand to hop to it as a whole, it used to be dropped entirely; now the alternating fingertip takes whichever chord note is on its side, salvaging one of the two.

**Validation.** Real-arm evaluation twice at 100% with timing spread 2 to 8 ms; simulated zigzag streams still fully played.
